I whispered one sentence to
Molly, who runs the café:

the festival stage was thrown
together from old planks.

Within the hour, the police
chief had taped it off,

the organizer had slipped on a banana peel,
and the town reporter smelled a scoop.

In VIRAL, you're not a character.
You're a thought that spreads.

Mistport's Lantern Festival starts at
eight. Pick anyone. Whisper anything.

We built the town: eight residents with
secrets, grudges and a festival to run.
Gemma, running on AMD, plays each of them.

They only know what
they've seen and heard,

and they decide for themselves what
to believe and what to do.

Same town. A different
sentence. A different evening.

And sometimes, nobody cares.
That's allowed too.

The game checks every answer, decides what
actually happens, and keeps the receipts.
Every event traces back to its cause.

At eight o'clock, you see what your
sentence did. Then you read all about it.

A full story costs less than

It's made for players who
love social sandboxes,

and for streamers whose
audience writes the sentence.
One sentence. A whole town.
